text.p: Singapore's media group Singapore Press Holdings (SPH) announced disappointing earnings on Friday for the full year ended August 31 1996, below analysts' expectations.
It said its net profit fell 1.1 percent to Singapore $307.63 million (US$218 million).
This is below analysts' forecasts of growth of between two and eight percent.

SPH said on Friday its earnings were impacted by high newsprint prices which were on average 50.7 percent higher than the previous financial year. It said advertising revenue only grew 6.9 percent, impacted by Singapore's slower economic growth.
Profit before tax was down 0.06 percent to S$423.56 million.
SPH recommended a final dividend of 20 cents per share, unchanged from last year.
SPH said circulation revenue grew by 8.5 percent. The group's trading profit grew by a marginal 0.1 percent to S$377.58 million.
Chairman Lim Kim San told reporters at a briefing that the group expected flat earnings for 1997.
"It depends on the economy. If the economy maintains here, I think we should have about the same returns," Lim said.
He said although newsprint prices had stabilised at about US$650 per tonne, cheaper than last year, wage costs had risen.
He said the group's new presses which would be operational by January 1997, would yield more colour advertisements and might improve advertising revenue.
Lim said the group's newspaper circulation grew by 1.7 percent for fiscal year 1996. "As far as newspaper circulation is concerned we have reached maturity," he added.

He said the group's multimedia business was key to its future growth but he did not expect substantial contributions to earnings from this segment until the year 2000. He added the group had invested in properties and other investments and future earnings would be impacted by these.
